 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That On 7-2-2012 at about 8.55 p.m., the petitioner was riding Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-50/4266 on Thindlu main road, when he reached near Lake Share Garden, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-39/4767, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
As a result of which, the said accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to M.S.Ramaih hospital,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses etc.
3.
It is contended that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 45 years and working as an office boy at L & T Comatsu Ltd., and earning Rs.6,500/-p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as earlier and also lost his earning capacity.
4. It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA- 39/4767.
Hence, case has been registered by the jurisdictional Hebbal Traffic Police in Cr.No.16/2012 against driver of said vehicle.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
5. In response to issuance of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 were appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statements.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Car bearing registration No.KA-39/4767 this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Further took contention that, driver of offending vehicle did not posses valid and effective D.L. as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is further contended that, the offending vehicle is not involved in the accident, the police have falsely implicated the same in the alleged accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

Ultimately, stated that the compensation claimed by Vasanth Kumar vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3410147/
2 the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.

sentences.text: With all these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further stated that he is the owner of car bearing registration No.KA-39/4767 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.1 and policy was in force as on the date of the accident.
Further stated that driver had valid and effective D.L. as on the date of the accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately, stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that was taken place on 07-02-2012, at about 8.55 a.m near Lake Share Garden, Thindlu road, Bengaluru, involving vehicle bearing registration No.KA-39/4767 belonging to Respondent No.2 and insured with Respondent No.1?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that the accident has mainly occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the said vehicle?
3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation from the respondents, if so what is the quantum?
4. What order?
9. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 & Ex.P12.

Further he has examined Sri.Gopalappa H.M. the Medical Record Officer of M.S.Ramaiah hospital as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex-P13 and Ex.P14.
10.

On the other hand, the Administrative officer of the respondent No.1 insurance company is examined as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
11.

After hearing the arguments on merits, my predecessor in office, dismissed the claim petition filed by the petitioner on 16.01.2015.
12.
Subsequently, the petitioner being aggrieved by the said judgment preferred an appeal as per M.F.A No.8812/2015 before the Honourable High court of Karnataka Bengaluru.

The said appeal came to be allowed and judgment passed by this court was set aside and the matter was remanded back to the Tribunal to the stage of further evidence of the petitioner and also directed to pass an Vasanth Kumar vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3410147/

sentences.text: 3 order in accordance with law by directing this court, to give an opportunity to both the parties, to adduce further evidence, in support of their respective contentions.
13. After remanding the matter, notice was issued to both the parties, to comply the direction of the Honourable High court of Karnataka.
On 1.10.2024, the learned counsel for the petitioner and the respondent No.1 were appeared before the court.
14. Inspite of granting sufficient time, neither the petitioner nor the respondents have adduced oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.

15. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
16.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Negative  Issue No.2: In the Negative  Issue No.3: Does not survive for  consideration  Issue No.4: As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1 & 2:-
17.
These two issues are taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts.

18. It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-30-4767 the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
19. On the other hand, the respondents have disputed that the accident has occurred not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

20. On the basis of rival contentions of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
Then onus shifts on the respondents.
21. The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the police documents Ex.P1 to Ex.P6.

Ex.P1-true copy of the F.I.R. along with complaint, Ex.P2-true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P3-true copy of charge sheet,
Ex.P4-true copy of sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of mahazar and Ex.P6-true copy of IMV report.

4 22.

sentences.text: On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one T.V.Nagesh, the S.H.O., Hebbal Traffic Police Station has registered the case in Cr.No.16/2012 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, I.O. has filed the charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
23.
On the contrary, the respondent No.1 has examined Administrative Officer of the insurance company as RW1.

He has deposed in his evidence that the petitioner has colluded with the police to lodge a false police complaint and got prepared all the documents in his favour, but the medical documents produced by the petitioner shows that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to self fall and was consumed alcohol at the time of driving.

24. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, has admitted that he was riding two wheeler, there was no vehicle in between his two wheeler and Tata indica car, he has observed Tata indica car at a distance of 10 feet.
Further denied the suggestion that he has sustained injuries due to self fall and Tata indica car was not involved in the accident.

25. In support of the stand of the petitioner has examined RMO of M.S. Ramaiah hospital,
Bengaluru.
He has placed outpatient record and inpatient record as per Ex.P13 & Ex.P14.

In the cross-examination he has stated that, he do not know who has written in the history column at Ex.P14.
26.

The counsel for the petitioner has filed the written arguments and argued that the petitioner being rider of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-50-K- 4266 was riding his vehicle carefully and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations at that moment, all of a sudden one car bearing No.KA- 39-4767 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner without controlling the vehicle taking sudden full right turn came to extrame right and hit the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to the impact the petitioner fell down and sustained multiple fractures.
27. Per contra the counsel for the respondent No.1 has argued that the accident has occurred, not due to the negligent act of the driver of the car.
As per the medical documents produced by the petitioner, itself is clear that the accident has occurred due to self fall by the petitioner under the influence of alcohol.
Ex.P13 & Ex.P14 clearly reflects that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the self fall under the influence of alcohol.

28. On going through the rival contentions of both the parties, it is necessary to rely Ex.P14 in the column History, which indicates that "RTA @ 8.50 p.m. on 7.2.2011 with self fall of two wheeler Vidyaraynapura Bangalore sustaining injury to face, under the influence of alcohol".
29.
To disprove the said fact, the petitioner has not made an effort to examine the author of the document and also not made an effort to clarify the accident date as as mentioned in Ex.P14.
Though he has examined PW3, but his evidence will not much helpful to disprove the contents of Ex.P14.
Further he has not examined the complainant, who lodged the complaint on 7.2.2012.

5 30.

sentences.text: Moreover, on perusal of IMV report clearly reveals that, there is no visible damages found in both the vehicle.
If the driver of the car hit the petitioner's vehicle, at least one of the vehicle would have caused damage, but as per IMV report there is no visible damages found.
On perusal of the charge sheet marked at Ex.P3 police have charge sheeted the driver of the car for the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
Mere filing of charge sheet against the driver of the car is not a ground to accept the version of the petitioner.

31. Over all appreciation of the evidence of PW1, PW3 & RW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioner has failed to establish that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-39-4767.
Hence, I am answering the issue No.1 & 2 in the Negative.

ISSUE No.3:
32.
The petitioner has failed to establish that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Tata indica car.
Therefore, respondent No.1 & 2 are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, answering the issue No.3 does not survive for consideration.

ISSUE No.4:
33.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
